title: Streamlined SDK error layer: enriched error contexts and cross-language codes
creator: Rajat Singh
description: Problem: SDK users across Python/TS/Go see inconsistent error shapes, sparse retry hints, and poor streaming resume ergonomics. This makes automated retries fragile, developer debugging slow, and client libraries hard to reason about for production workloads. Goal: introduce a thin, language-idiomatic error layer that standardizes machine-readable error codes, preserves rich runtime context (request_id, model_variant, kv_prefix_hit, resume_token), and surfaces actionable human messages and retryability hints. Deliverables: a) public error schema spec (code, category, retry_hint, http_status, stable_error_id, telemetry_tag) b) language wrappers that translate runtime transport errors into that schema with lightweight helpers (is_retryable(), get_resume_token(), to_log_entry()) c) streaming contract for resumable and resumable-adjacent failures d) examples and migration guidance for existing customers.
acceptance_criteria: Publish error schema doc in SDK repo and Console docs: fields, semantics, and example JSON payloads
Python/TS/Go SDKs expose ErrorWithContext type that includes stable_error_id, code, category, retry_hint (none/soft/hard), http_status, request_id, model_variant, route, and optional resume_token
is_retryable() helper returns true only for transient categories and soft retry_hints; contains guidance for idempotency requirements
Streaming APIs include explicit ResumeToken extraction method and example snippet showing checkpoint+resume flow
Telemetry payloads include telemetry_tag and stable_error_id for server-side grouping; SDK attaches minimal stable metadata to every error event
Backward compatibility: existing catch-all exceptions preserved but include new context fields when available; no breaking change for basic try/except usage
End-to-end tests covering transient error -> retry logic, streaming resume, and translation from HTTP 502/503/504 to SDK retryable errors
implementation_notes: Design a small core error code list: INTERNAL, INVALID_ARGUMENT, UNAUTHORIZED, PERMISSION_DENIED, NOT_FOUND, RATE_LIMIT, CAPACITY_EXHAUSTED, TIMEOUT, CANCELLED, STREAM_TRUNCATED, RESUMABLE_STATE_LOST
Map HTTP status ranges: 5xx -> candidate transient (special-case 501/505 as hard), 4xx -> client errors except 429 -> RATE_LIMIT
Introduce stable_error_id generated server-side for grouping; SDK surfaces it as stable_error_id for diagnostics
Retry hint enum: none | soft | hard. soft means safe to retry with default backoff; hard means user intervention likely required (e.g., invalid prompt schema)

Streaming: adopt resume_token semantics where the server returns token in error payload when it can resume; SDKs should attempt automated resume only if the user provides idempotency key OR the API is idempotent for the operation

Provide small language-specific ergonomic helpers: Python context manager for streaming sessions that auto-snapshot last_acked_token; TS async iterator wrapper that preserves checkpoint; Go client returns a ResumeAccessor interface
Telemetry: attach 'telemetry_tag' and 'stable_error_id' to SDK logs and optional user-configurable telemetry hook. Avoid PII in error messages.
rollout_plan: Phase 1: spec and server-side error payloads behind a feature flag (runtime-err-schema). Phase 2: ship Python and TS helpers as opt-in runtime flags and add Go prototype. Phase 3: flip opt-in to default, add migration docs and SDK changelog entries. Coordinate with Console to surface stable_error_id in error detail pages and with runtime team to include resume_token when resumable. Watchlist: customer-facing churn on behavior changes; provide opt-out flag for strict legacy behavior.
